case_title: Gurpal Singh v. State of Punjab
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (brother of the informant, who was shot at); prior land dispute between the brothers; the deceased was a friend of the informant's son
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; IPC s.307 (charged). Final conviction under IPC s.304 Part I and s.307
evidence_type: Eyewitness; medical; recovery (gun and cartridges); site plan; cartridge shells recovered from spot
aggravating_circumstances: Firing at several persons within sight, causing one death and several injuries
mitigating_circumstances: Sudden uncontrollable anger; root cause of incident and events that unfolded; twelve-year lapse since occurrence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302 (life imprisonment, fine Rs.5,000) and s.307 (five years RI, fine Rs.2,000); sentences concurrent; co-accused acquitted
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 378-DB of 2004) dismissed; conviction and sentence affirmed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.304 Part I (culpable homicide not amounting to murder); IPC s.307 (attempt to murder)
neutral_facts: Two adjacent households, whose members were brothers, had a long-running dispute over land. On the day in question, the son of one household was working in the fields when the accused hurled abuses at him. The son returned home upset and complained to his father. The father went to the rooftop of his house and called the accused over. The accused came with his own son. When the father asked why the accused had abused his son, the accused replied angrily that he was justified and would continue. The accused then ran downstairs, fetched a double-barrelled 12-bore gun and fired at the father, striking him on the side of the head. It was alleged that the accused's son urged the firing. Hearing the commotion, the father's wife and two friends of the son rushed to the rooftop. The accused fired at them. One friend was struck in the abdomen and died, the father's wife was struck in the abdomen, and the other friend was struck in the mouth and head. The injured were taken to hospital, where the friend who was struck died. The accused and his son then fled. In the investigation, the 12-bore gun loaded with two live cartridges was recovered from the accused, and four cartridge shells were recovered from the spot. The site plan prepared by the investigating officer matched the eyewitnesses' account of the place of occurrence. The eyewitnesses included the father and the injured. The medical evidence showed injuries on the deceased and the injured compatible with the weapon used.
physical_harm: Death of one friend (Jatinder Singh); gunshot wound to the informant's head side; gunshot injuries to the informant's wife (abdomen) and to Lakhwinder (mouth and head)
number_of_offences: 2 charged; 2 finally upheld (s.302 modified to s.304 Part I; s.307 upheld)
premeditation_planning: Not found. Court held the firing followed an uncontrollable fit of anger and did not show intention to eliminate any person.
motive: alleged: lingering land dispute between the brothers, with the abuse of the informant's son as the immediate trigger
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of the informant and injured witnesses; recovery of the 12-bore gun with live cartridges from the accused; four cartridge shells recovered from the spot; site plan; medical evidence compatible with the weapon
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses, including the informant, found consistent, coherent and convincing, and trustworthy; family relationship plea rejected
post_offence_conduct: Fled the scene after the firing (as alleged in the prosecution account; not separately found by the court)
trial_duration: offence: 06.07.2002 (judgment also refers to the occurrence as being of the year 2004 at page 5); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 01.10.2008; Supreme Court: 02.12.2016
legal_representation: Appellant: Yatinder Singh, Senior Advocate (Amicus Curiae), with Arijeet Singh and Ms. Aprajita Anvita, Advocates. State: Saurabh Ajay Gupta, AAG, with Ms. Naresh Bakshi, Saurabh Singhal and Nishant Bishnoi, Advocates.
investigation_status: FIR registered on the informant's statement; investigation completed; charge-sheet laid under ss.302 and 307 IPC; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial Court: convicted under ss.302 and 307 IPC, sentenced. High Court (Criminal Appeal No. 378-DB of 2004): dismissed; conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal partly allowed; conviction converted to ss.304 Part I and 307 IPC; sentence reduced to period undergone.
prosecution_argument: Injured eyewitness testimony, supported by medical evidence, proved the charge beyond reasonable doubt; concurrent findings of the lower courts should not be disturbed
defence_argument: Prosecution failed to prove the charge; the co-accused's acquittal undermines the case; eyewitnesses are related and partisan; in the alternative, even if accepted, no murder or attempt to murder was proved and the sentence should be reduced
legal_principle_applied: Evaluation of eyewitness reliability and medical corroboration; acquittal of co-accused does not bear on the appellant's guilt; distinction between intention to kill and knowledge of likely fatal consequences, leading to s.304 Part I
sentencing_rationale: Singular facts, root cause of the incident, sequence of events, uncontrollable anger, lack of intention to eliminate, and the twelve-year lapse since the occurrence, taken together meet the ends of justice
judicial_mitigating_factors: Overpowered by uncontrollable anger; root cause and sequence of events; time lag of twelve years since the occurrence
other_sentence_order: Appellant to be set at liberty forthwith unless required in any other case
